newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan pulls the plug on '24-hour' bathtubs.
newsitem.headline: Japan pulls the plug on '24-hour' bathtubs.

text.p: The Japanese are world-renowned for their love of hot tubs, so it was only natural that they would take to "24-hour" baths, which offer the chance to take a soak at any time around the clock.
But fears that a pneumonia-causing bacteria could be unleashed in the self-purifying units have prompted three companies to stop selling the popular bathtubs.
The tub circulates and purifies the bath water through a self-contained system so that the bath is filled with fresh, warm water day and night.
But government officials, concerned that the legionella pneumophila bacterium could grow in the system, contaminating the water, now want to take a second look at the luxury.
In a statement on Monday, the Trade Ministry said it has asked manufacturers to check the safety of their products, and will meet with a panel of bathing experts before deciding if sales can resume.
Companies said they were hopeful that the bad news would wash away.
"We have stopped selling '24-hour bath' units but the decision is only temporary," said a spokesman from Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, one of the firms to suspend sales.
